rules.when: The task is design, architecture, product framing, or asking the captain clarifying questions: system shape, API boundaries, tradeoff analysis, Lavish planning judgment, or Explore-mode hard questions. Not bulk implementation.
rules.why: Fable owns judgment, design, and architecture. Do not burn Cursor/Codex as the first pick for open design decisions.

rules.when: The task is frontend taste or layout cleanup: polish visual hierarchy, spacing, brand feel, or converge after exploratory UI variants. Not a bulk fan-out of many rough options.
rules.why: Fable owns taste/layout convergence after faster models generate options.

rules.when: The task is exploratory UI or Paper fan-out: generate several rough variants or surfaces quickly so the captain can compare, not a final taste pass.
rules.why: Speed-class fan-out. Cursor first (no effort flag on Cursor); Codex next. Save Fable for later convergence.

rules.when: The task is a chore: docs, CI hygiene, Linear hygiene, renames, formatting, dependency bumps, or other low-ambiguity housekeeping.
rules.why: Fastest cheap path. Cursor first; Codex fallback.

rules.when: The task is a trivial mechanical edit: targeted typo, one-file fix, rote rename, or similarly narrow low-ambiguity coding.
The task is adversarial review, no-mistakes review, or a second-opinion pass on code another model authored.
rules.why: Prefer a different family than the author. Codex is the standing review default; Claude only if Codex is tight.

rules.when: The task is a big or ambiguous multi-file feature or risky refactor where architecture is already decided and the work is primarily implementation with remaining technical ambiguity.
rules.why: Codex is the mid/frontier implementer (smarter than pure speed, faster than Fable). Cursor second. Claude last to conserve Fable/Claude quota.

rules.when: The task is an ordinary ship: feature slice, bug fix, or refactor with clear acceptance criteria and limited ambiguity.
rules.why: Default implementation path. Cursor for speed; Codex when Cursor headroom is tight or the slice needs more frontier punch.
